title: Contraception
content:
# Contraception

## Learning Objectives
By the end of this lesson, you should be able to:
- Describe different methods of contraception
- Explain how hormonal contraceptives work
- Compare the effectiveness of different contraceptive methods
- Understand how fertility treatments work

## Introduction

**Contraception** refers to methods used to prevent pregnancy. Understanding contraception requires knowledge of the menstrual cycle and how hormones control reproduction. Some methods also have medical uses beyond contraception.

## Key Concepts

### Types of Contraception

**Main categories:**

| Category | Examples | How they work |
|----------|----------|---------------|
| Barrier | Condoms, diaphragm | Physically block sperm |
| Hormonal | Pill, implant, injection | Alter hormone levels |
| Intrauterine | IUD, IUS | Prevent implantation |
| Natural | Rhythm method, withdrawal | Avoid fertile period |
| Permanent | Sterilisation | Surgery to prevent conception |

### Barrier Methods

#### Male Condom

**How it works:**
- Thin latex/polyurethane sheath worn over penis
- Prevents sperm entering vagina
- Collects ejaculated semen

**Effectiveness:** ~98% with perfect use, ~85% typical use

**Advantages:**
- Protects against STIs
- No hormones
- Easily available
- Male-controlled

**Disadvantages:**
- Can break or slip
- Interrupts spontaneity
- Requires correct use each time

#### Female Condom

**How it works:**
- Pouch inserted into vagina
- Lines vaginal walls
- Prevents sperm reaching egg

**Effectiveness:** ~95% with perfect use

#### Diaphragm/Cap

**How it works:**
- Dome of silicone placed over cervix
- Used with spermicide
- Blocks sperm entering uterus

**Effectiveness:** ~92-96% with perfect use

### Hormonal Methods

#### Combined Oral Contraceptive Pill

**Contains:** Oestrogen and progesterone (synthetic versions)

**How it works:**

| Hormone | Effect |
|---------|--------|
| Oestrogen | Inhibits FSH → no follicle development |
| Progesterone | Inhibits LH → no ovulation |
| Both | Thicken cervical mucus → sperm can't pass |
| Both | Thin uterus lining → implantation less likely |

**Effectiveness:** >99% with perfect use

**Advantages:**
- Very effective
- Can reduce period pain
- Regulates periods
- Reduces some cancer risks

**Disadvantages:**
- Must be taken daily
- Side effects in some women
- Does not protect against STIs
- Small increased risk of blood clots

#### Progesterone-Only Pill (Mini Pill)

**Contains:** Progesterone only

**How it works:**
- Thickens cervical mucus
- Thins uterus lining
- May prevent ovulation (some types)

**Effectiveness:** ~99% with perfect use

**Advantages:**
- Can be used by women who can't take oestrogen
- Suitable while breastfeeding

**Disadvantages:**
- Must be taken at same time daily
- Irregular bleeding

#### Contraceptive Injection

**How it works:**
- Slow-release progesterone
- Given every 8-13 weeks
- Prevents ovulation
- Thickens cervical mucus

**Effectiveness:** >99%

**Advantages:**
- Long-lasting
- Don't need to remember daily

**Disadvantages:**
- Cannot be reversed quickly
- May cause irregular bleeding
- May delay return to fertility

#### Contraceptive Implant

**How it works:**
- Small rod inserted under skin of arm
- Releases progesterone slowly
- Lasts up to 3 years
- Prevents ovulation, thickens mucus

**Effectiveness:** >99%

**Advantages:**
- Very effective
- Long-lasting (3 years)
- Reversible

**Disadvantages:**
- Requires minor procedure
- May cause irregular bleeding

#### Contraceptive Patch

**How it works:**
- Patch worn on skin
- Releases oestrogen and progesterone
- Changed weekly

**Effectiveness:** ~99%

### Intrauterine Devices

#### IUD (Copper Coil)

**How it works:**
- Small T-shaped device in uterus
- Copper is toxic to sperm
- Creates inflammatory response
- Prevents fertilisation and implantation

**Effectiveness:** >99%

**Duration:** 5-10 years

**Advantages:**
- No hormones
- Long-lasting
- Can be used as emergency contraception

#### IUS (Hormonal Coil)

**How it works:**
- T-shaped device releasing progesterone
- Thins uterus lining
- Thickens cervical mucus

**Effectiveness:** >99%

**Duration:** 3-5 years

### Natural Methods

#### Calendar/Rhythm Method

**How it works:**
- Track menstrual cycle
- Avoid intercourse during fertile days
- Requires regular cycles

**Effectiveness:** ~76-88%

**Disadvantages:**
- Requires careful tracking
- Less reliable with irregular cycles
- No STI protection

### Permanent Methods (Sterilisation)

| Method | Procedure | Notes |
|--------|-----------|-------|
| Vasectomy (male) | Cutting/blocking vas deferens | Should be considered permanent |
| Tubal ligation (female) | Cutting/blocking fallopian tubes | More complex surgery |

**Effectiveness:** >99%

### Emergency Contraception

#### Emergency Hormonal Pill

**How it works:**
- High dose of progesterone
- Delays or prevents ovulation
- Must be taken within 72 hours (some types 120 hours)

#### Emergency IUD

**How it works:**
- Copper IUD inserted within 5 days
- Prevents implantation
- Most effective emergency method

### Fertility Treatments

**When natural conception is difficult:**

#### FSH Treatment

**Used when:** Woman doesn't ovulate regularly

**How it works:**
- FSH injections stimulate follicle development
- Eggs mature and are released
- Can cause multiple eggs (risk of multiple pregnancy)

#### IVF (In Vitro Fertilisation)

**Process:**
1. FSH given to stimulate egg production
2. Eggs collected from ovaries
3. Eggs fertilised with sperm in laboratory
4. Embryos develop for few days
5. Embryo(s) transferred to uterus
6. Hormone support for implantation

**Success rate:** ~20-35% per cycle (varies with age)

**Issues:**
- Expensive
- Emotionally demanding
- Multiple births risk
- Ethical questions about unused embryos

### Comparing Methods

| Method | Effectiveness | STI Protection | Hormone-free |
|--------|--------------|----------------|-------------|
| Combined pill | >99% | No | No |
| Condom | 85-98% | Yes | Yes |
| IUD | >99% | No | Yes |
| Implant | >99% | No | No |
| Natural methods | 76-88% | No | Yes |

## Common Exam Questions

- Explain how the contraceptive pill prevents pregnancy
- Compare different methods of contraception
- Describe how FSH is used in fertility treatment
- Explain the process of IVF

## Common Misconceptions

- **Misconception:** The pill causes infertility
- **Reality:** Fertility returns after stopping the pill

- **Misconception:** Contraception is 100% effective
- **Reality:** No method is 100% effective; effectiveness varies

- **Misconception:** Only barrier methods are available without prescription
- **Reality:** Some hormonal methods are available from pharmacies

- **Misconception:** IVF always works
- **Reality:** Success rates are around 20-35% per cycle

## Practice Questions

1. State two methods of hormonal contraception. (2 marks)

2. Explain how the combined oral contraceptive pill prevents pregnancy. (4 marks)

3. Compare the use of condoms with hormonal contraception. (4 marks)

4. Describe how FSH is used to treat infertility. (3 marks)

5. Explain the process of IVF. (4 marks)

6. Discuss the advantages and disadvantages of different contraceptive methods. (6 marks)

## Key Terms Glossary

| Term | Definition |
|------|------------|
| Contraception | Methods to prevent pregnancy |
| Barrier method | Contraception that physically blocks sperm |
| Hormonal contraception | Uses hormones to prevent pregnancy |
| IUD | Intrauterine device (copper coil) |
| IUS | Intrauterine system (hormonal coil) |
| IVF | In vitro fertilisation |
| Sterilisation | Permanent surgical contraception |
| Emergency contraception | Contraception used after intercourse |
| Fertility treatment | Medical help to achieve pregnancy |

## Summary

- Contraception prevents pregnancy through various mechanisms
- Barrier methods physically block sperm (condoms, diaphragm)
- Hormonal methods alter hormone levels (pill, implant, injection)
- Combined pill contains oestrogen and progesterone; prevents ovulation
- IUD/IUS are long-acting reversible methods
- FSH can be used to stimulate ovulation in fertility treatment
- IVF involves fertilisation outside the body
- Different methods have different effectiveness and side effects
